title: Composite-void urinary creatinine rate does not establish incremental grip-strength prediction beyond concentration and urine flow across NHANES cohorts
abstract: We tested a composite-void urinary creatinine excretion-rate proxy as a concurrent combined-handgrip predictor in adults20–79. An additive spline ridge model trained in NHANES2011–2012 (n=3794) was evaluated without recalibration in separately recruited2013–2014 participants (n=4191). Beyond age, sex, race/ethnicity, BMI, height, serum creatinine, urine albumin/creatinine ratio and urine creatinine concentration, adding log-rate splines changed examination-weighted MSE by -1.1854 kg² (joint source/target PSU-bootstrap95% interval [-3.2746,+1.1426]). With log urine flow also in the comparator, the delta was +0.3174 kg² [-1.0647,+2.9918]. The registered improvement criterion failed. This exploratory reused-cohort negative result does not exclude physiological associations or validate a muscle-mass biomarker. Independent-program validation was not completed.
